basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE SEAT OF GOVERNMENT OF THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF PARANG, PROVINCE OF MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING BOOK 1, CHAPTER 2, SECTION 9 OF THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 13, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or in two newspapers of general circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Moves the region's capital. The seat of government of the BARMM is established at Parang, Maguindanao del Norte, where a new government centre will be built — with the transfer from Cotabato City to happen gradually as the infrastructure is finished.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act rests on the region's power to organise its own bureaucracy in the exercise of self-governance. It gives no further reason for the choice of location.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The Wali's office, the Chief Minister's office, the Parliament, the ministries and agencies are all to relocate to a new government centre at Parang. A committee chaired by the Senior Minister plans it, Parliament approves the site, and the whole project has a ten-year limit.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of Parang, Maguindanao del Norte, where the new capital will sit
Cotabato City, which loses the seat of government
Anyone who travels to the regional government for services
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2023, but the physical transfer is gradual and depends on infrastructure being built.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The region's capital moves from Cotabato City to Parang, Maguindanao del Norte — gradually, as buildings, roads, power and water are completed, with a ten-year outer limit on the project.
in_practice: The seat of government is established at Parang, where the Bangsamoro government centre will be built
It will house the Office of the Wali, the Office of the Chief Minister, the Parliament, ministries, offices and agencies
A Committee on the Establishment of the Seat of Government, chaired by the Senior Minister, plans the move and identifies the site — subject to Parliament's approval
Civil society organisations are invited as observers to the Committee
The physical transfer from Cotabato City proceeds gradually as office buildings, roads, light and power, water and communications are completed
The existing government centre in Cotabato City is to be improved and preserved for its historical value, and renamed after the transfer
₱50,000,000 for the first year, with later amounts through the annual budget; foreign grants and donations are permitted
The Committee dissolves on completion, and in any case within 10 years unless Parliament extends it

for_specific_groups.Residents of Parang: The regional capital comes to your municipality — but Section 4 excludes the government centre from local policies that would run counter to uninterrupted government service.
for_specific_groups.Cotabato City: You lose the seat of government. The existing centre is to be improved, preserved for its historical value, and renamed once the move is complete.
for_specific_groups.Government employees: Relocation is gradual and tied to infrastructure, not to a fixed date.
for_specific_groups.Civil society: CSO representatives are invited as observers to the planning committee — a rare express seat, though as observers rather than members.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: Parang, Maguindanao del Norte, and the existing government centre in Cotabato City.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Gradually. The transfer depends on completed infrastructure, with a ten-year outer limit on the Committee's life.
what_you_can_do: Ask the Committee on the Establishment of the Seat of Government about the master plan and timetable
Note that the specific site requires Parliament's approval
Ask about the consultations with local government units the act requires
watch_out_for: Section 4 removes the government centre from the reach of local policies that would run counter to uninterrupted government service — a significant carve-out from municipal authority.
No completion deadline for the transfer itself; only the Committee has a ten-year limit, extendable by Parliament.
₱50 million is a first-year planning figure, not the cost of building a capital.
The act gives no stated reason for choosing Parang.

key_terms_explained.Seat of government: Where the region's central institutions are located.
key_terms_explained.Wali: The ceremonial head of the Bangsamoro.
key_terms_explained.CESG: Committee on the Establishment of the Seat of Government, which plans and oversees the move.
key_terms_explained.Inter-Governmental Fiscal Policy Board: The joint national–regional body whose guidelines govern foreign grants and donations here.

everyday_scenarios: A resident of Parang finds the regional capital being built in their municipality. The government centre will not be subject to local policies that would interrupt government service, and consultations with the LGU are required.
A government employee in Cotabato City asks when they must move. The transfer is gradual and begins only as office buildings, roads, power, water and communications are completed.
Someone asks what happens to the old centre. It is to be improved, preserved for its historical value, and renamed once the transfer is complete, with stakeholders consulted on the new name.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Seat of Government Act of 2023”. The act amends Book 1, Chapter 2, Section 9 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 13, the Bangsamoro Administrative Code.

Section 2 — Policy: in exercising its right to self-governance the region is free to pursue its political, economic, social and cultural development, and has the power to create offices and organise its own bureaucracy for efficient and effective delivery of government programmes and services.

Section 3 — Establishes the seat of the BARMM in the Municipality of Parang, Maguindanao del Norte, where the Bangsamoro government centre shall be built, housing the Office of the Wali, the Office of the Chief Minister, the Bangsamoro Parliament, ministries, offices and agencies, and other facilities.

Section 4 — The government centre within Parang shall not be subject to local policies, measures and issuances that would run counter to the primacy of uninterrupted government service. Consultations and dialogues with the local government unit and other stakeholders shall be conducted to ensure a smooth transition.

Section 5 — Establishes the Committee on the Establishment of the Seat of Government, chaired by the Senior Minister, with the Ministers of Finance and Budget and Management, Public Works, Environment, Natural Resources and Energy, and Transportation and Communications; the Chairperson of the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage; and the Director-General of the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority. Civil society organisations' representatives are invited as observers. The Committee identifies the specific site and area, subject to the approval of Parliament; convenes within 30 days of effectivity; and ceases to exist on completion and full implementation, which shall not exceed 10 years unless extended by Parliament.

Section 6 — The actual physical transfer from Cotabato City to Parang proceeds gradually upon completion of required infrastructure — office buildings, roads, light and power, water, communication and other facilities. The Committee leads preparation of the master plan, strategies, processes and timetable, including identification of the site for the Parliament, and conducts consultations with concerned local government units and stakeholders.

Section 7 — The infrastructure, buildings and facilities of the existing government centre in Cotabato City shall be improved to sustain their usefulness for government operations and preserve their historical value. The present centre shall be renamed after the final transfer is completed, with stakeholders consulted on the new name.

Section 8 — ₱50,000,000 is initially appropriated for the Committee's first year, including crafting the master plan; later amounts go through the General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro. Foreign grants, aids and donations may also be used, subject to the guidelines of the Inter-Governmental Fiscal Policy Board.
Section 9 — The Committee, consulting appropriate agencies, shall promulgate implementing rules within 90 days of effectivity.
Section 12 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or in two newspapers of general circulation.

citizen_questions.a: Yes. The seat of government is established at Parang, Maguindanao del Norte, where a new Bangsamoro government centre will be built to house the Wali, the Chief Minister, the Parliament, and the ministries and agencies.
Gradually, as the required infrastructure — office buildings, roads, power, water and communications — is completed. The act sets no completion date; only the planning Committee has a ten-year limit.
The Committee on the Establishment of the Seat of Government identifies the specific site and area, subject to the approval of the Bangsamoro Parliament.
The existing government centre is to be improved and preserved for its historical value, and renamed once the transfer is complete, with stakeholders consulted on the new name.

₱50 million was appropriated for the Committee's first year including the master plan. The cost of actually building the capital is left to later budgets, with foreign grants and donations also permitted.

citizen_questions.q: Will Parang's local government control the site?
citizen_questions.a: Not entirely. Section 4 says the government centre shall not be subject to local policies, measures and issuances that would run counter to the primacy of uninterrupted government service.
